glossary.definition: An identity for software, such as an AI agent, rather than a person. In Privilege it is either an agent access key tied to a custodian, or a NonHumanIdentity that proves itself with a platform token and holds no static secret.
The key an agent sends as a Bearer token on every call. It is the whole identity of the agent: it names a custodian and carries scopes, limits, a guardrail and an expiry.
The human an agent key acts as. Policy is issued to the custodian and the gateway log names them. If the custodian goes inactive, the key stops working.
The policy Privilege creates when apps are selected on a key. Selecting the app is the grant; for MCP apps the grant can list individual tools.
The coarse gate on a key: llm, mcp or a2a. A key can only use the gateway surfaces it has a scope for.
The guardrail screen configured on a key, not on an app. It is the only screen on agent-to-agent calls. Defaults mostly alert rather than block.
The five checks the gateway runs in order on every call: key valid, scope granted, app or model granted, within limits, guardrail passes. Each failure has its own status code.
